Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

responsible adjective

to blame, at fault

also to blame, be to blame, at fault, it’s my fault, whose fault is it?, be responsible for (something bad), I don’t blame you, blame someone, hold it against someone, push the blame on, shift the blame, blame, I am to blame, blame someone for, fault, not at fault, not be at fault, not my fault, be guilty

classical

Ter. Hec. 4.4.78: is quidem in culpā nōn est (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 8.6.3 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 98
Traupman 193, 195
Traupman 313
Traupman 324

in culpā esse

phrase: in + ablative of culpa, with esse

to be to blame, be at fault

The plain way to say who is to blame. Turned round, mea culpa est is “it’s my fault” (Cic. Brut. 133).

Other words

  • culpa est penes (aliquem) — the blame lies with someone

    phrase: penes + accusative · also used · classical · Liv. 35.33.3: penes Aetōlōs culpam bellī esse (Lewis & Short, s.v. culpa); Ter. Hec. 4.1.20: culpa, quae tē est penes

  • per aliquem stat (quōminus …) — it is someone’s doing (that something did not happen)

    phrase: per + accusative, mostly with quōminus or nē · also used · classical · Quint. 3.6.78: nōn per mē stetit, sed per illud (Lewis & Short, s.v. stō); Liv. 8.2.2 (Lewis & Short)

    Used of a hindrance: per eum stetit quōminus …, “it was his fault that … did not happen”. Rarely without a negative.

  • auctor, auctōris m. — the person who caused something, the one behind it

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sall. J. 1.4: suam quisque culpam auctōrēs ad negōtia trānsferunt (Lewis & Short)

    Not only an author: whoever brings a thing about, for good or ill, so the doer or instigator of an act; also of a woman (Lewis & Short, “comm.”). It names the person, not the fault.

  • vitiō vertere (alicui aliquid) — blame someone for something, hold it against him

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.6.1: nē sibi vitiō verterent, quod abesset ā patriā (Lewis & Short s.v. vitium)

    Literally “to turn (something) into a fault for someone”, with two datives. “I don’t blame you”: nōn tibi id vitiō vertō.

  • culpam in aliquem trānsferre — shift the blame onto someone

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 2.3.5; Cic. Att. 15.28 (Lewis & Short s.v. culpa); Traupman 94

    Traupman has culpam in aliquem cōnferre.

  • improperō, improperāre — reproach, blame

    verb, first conjugation · also used · post-classical · Petr. 38: nōn improperō illī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 94

    (vōx sermōnis vulgāris: Petr.; Vulg.)

    Lewis & Short: post-Augustan and very rare, found only in Petronius and the Vulgate (Rom. 15.3, Matt. 27.44). Traupman gives it for “I don’t blame you”.

  • culpa, culpae f. — blame, fault

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 5.6.10: quicquid hujus factumst culpā, nōn factumst meā (Lewis & Short); Traupman 193, 195; Traupman 313

  • culpō, culpāre, culpāvī, culpātum — blame, find fault with

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. culpō; Traupman 193

  • extrā culpam esse — not be at fault

    also used · classical · Liv. 8.19.10: aliquem extrā culpam bellī esse jūdicāre (Lewis & Short s.v. culpa); Traupman 313

Examples

  • Stultum est querī dē adversīs, ubi culpa est tua.

    It’s foolish to complain of bad luck when the fault is your own.Publ. S 45

  • mālō Tīrōnis verēcundiam in culpā esse quam inlīberālitātem Curiī

    I would rather Tiro’s shyness were to blame than Curius’s meannessCic. Att. 8.6.3

  • sed haec mea culpa est

    but this is my faultCic. Brut. 133

  • Nōn est in culpā canis; ego jānuam apertam relīquī.

    The dog isn’t to blame; I left the door open.composed

  • Atticae meae velim mē ita excūsēs ut omnem culpam in tē trānsferās

    please make my excuses to my Attica, and put all the blame on yourselfCic. Att. 15.28

  • Tibi nōn improperō.

    I don’t blame you.Traupman 94

  • In culpā sum.

    I am to blame.Traupman 193

  • aliquem culpāre ob aliquid

    to blame someone for somethingTraupman 193

  • extrā culpam esse

    not to be at faultTraupman 195

See also accept blame, in charge, responsible.
